meta.description: Performance cost map for TSL functions. Higher = more GPU cycles. Baseline: add = 1. SFU ops (sin/cos/sqrt/rcp) = 4 (quarter-rate on mobile GPUs). Budgets assume 3-5 shaders in scene. Noise family (voronoi/fbm) recalibrated 2026-07-23 from measured Adreno 740 (Quest 3) GPU-timestamp benchmarks (Static + MicroPlane agree); voronoi was ~4x underpriced. See ShaderCarousel/benchData/ (run data + METHODS.md). Image node repriced 2 -> 10 on 2026-09-09: it is AUTHORED, not measured (no bench atom samples a texture — see ShaderCarousel/lib/bench-registry.js, whose ops are all ALU), and at 2 it sat BELOW `colormap` (4), which samples a 1 KB LUT, while an Image node samples a mipmapped texture of up to ~16 MB (2048^2 RGBA8 at base level, ~22 MB with the mip chain — the 2048 the shipped Quest 3 profile caps drops at) — an ordering no GPU makes true. 10 = the texture-unit throughput the table already prices at 4 (independently estimated at ~3.6 pts for one trilinear fetch over the 2064x2208 reference at ~30 GTexel/s) plus a comparable term for the DRAM traffic a multi-megabyte texture pulls and a 1 KB LUT does not. It is the price of the LARGEST image the app produces, i.e. the conservative middle of a ~4 (cache-resident) to ~26 (every tap misses, DRAM-bound) band — and that band sweeps CACHE BEHAVIOUR for one fetch, not texture size: both endpoints are per-fragment rate statements with no dimension in them. THE PRICE ACTUALLY CHARGED IS SIZE-AWARE (utils/nodeCost.ts imageNodeCost, 2026-09-10): this entry is the ANCHOR, paid in full at 2048 px geometric-mean side and above, and DISCOUNTED log-linearly down to x0.5 at 256 px and below — 2048/1024/512/256 -> 10/8/7/5 — so the settings menu's Resolution ladder is consequential and no existing image reprices upward. A multiplier on this entry, never a literal, so a profile that overrides imageNode still moves every image node; junk or absent dimensions pay the flat entry; the floor stays strictly above colormap/sin. `dataNode` (2) and the stripes/dataviz/colormap LUT samplers are the same unmeasured class, and the coherence axis itself (the `data` colour space turns mipmaps off — the genuinely every-tap-misses case) is not priced yet. Measuring any of this needs a texture atom in the bench, which would need buildBenchRegistry to take THREE as well as TSL. `unknown` is a deliberate non-zero GUESS (no measurement is possible for a function the registry does not model): shaderloader 0.5 auto-imports any name that exists in THREE.TSL, so an unrecognised call RUNS, and codeToGraph wires none of its argument edges, so its upstream subtree also drops out of the reachable-cost BFS - 0 made the most expensive thing in such a graph read as free.
